blocks: prev:: and next:: link the notes a semitone below and above.
One H1 with the note name, then one line giving the MIDI note number, the frequency at A440, the flat spelling of a black key, and the name Live and Arturia use.
Music/Note/4/A, the 440 Hz tuning note. Music/Note/7/G, the low-battery chirp of Microfreak/Preset/399 FireAlarmLoBat. Music/Note/9/G, MIDI note 127, the top of the range.
The MIDI note number of a Logseq/Entity/Music/Note instance: an integer from 0 to 127, as in midi-note:: 69 on Music/Note/4/A.
MIDI note 60 is middle C, Music/Note/4/C. Each step of one is a semitone.
In this garden, Music Performance pages model a particular event or session in which a musical work is performed.
A performance is an occurrence, not the abstract work and not a recording of the occurrence.
A live rendition at a concert or awards show is a performance. An improvised studio or home session may also be modeled as a performance when it has a distinct identity worth revisiting.
An audio or video capture of the event is a separate Logseq/Entity/Music/Recording when the recording itself needs a page.
Place a performance under its principal performer as Person/<Performer>/Music/Performance/<Date or Event>/<Work>.
Use the event date or a stable event name to distinguish repeated performances of the same work.
A session of several works may use one event page with an ordered set of work:: links.
Use work:: for the performed work, performer:: for performers as defined at Logseq/Entity/Music/Recording/Frontmatter/performer, and recording:: for a recording page that documents the event.
Link an event or venue when its page exists. A performance's date-created:: is the date of the event when known.
Start each performance page with logseq-entity:: [[Logseq/Entity/Music/Performance]] and one H1 naming the performance.
Add the event date, work::, performers, and a source link when available.
In this garden, Music Recording pages model fixed audio or audiovisual recordings and album releases that preserve or publish musical material.
A recording is a captured rendition or a published collection of captured tracks. It has an identity apart from the musical work and any live performance it may document.

A studio track, a live album, and a video recording of a performance can each be recorded entities. An album page represents the release and its track order; a single-track page represents one captured rendition.
A recording of a cover is a new recording linked to the covered work. The cover does not create a new page for the underlying song.

Place a recording under its first credited Logseq/Entity/Identity/Music as <Identity>/Music/Recording/<Title> when Logseq/Frontmatter/created-by-identities is present. For a joint release, keep one page under the first credited identity and list all credited identities. Without a separate identity, use Person/<Artist>/Music/Recording/<Title>. Existing group namespaces remain valid until deliberately renamed.
Use the published album, single, track, or video title as the H1. Add a year or release context to distinguish recordings with the same title.

For an album, list known tracks as bullets under a Tracks heading, in listening order. Each track begins with its two-digit, zero-padded position and a hyphen, as 01 - Dis; the padding is two digits even on an album of nine tracks or fewer. A track links to its musical work page when that work is represented in the garden, and is plain text otherwise. Tracks are never page properties.
Use work:: for a single-work recording and performance:: when the recording documents a known performance event.
Album pages list tracks as numbered bullets. A work page may point back to an album with appears-on::.
Use cover-of:: to identify a recording as a cover of an existing work.
